change_notes.previous: Revision 1 froze register, pause, and replace under the mdm_administrator path, one active binding per scope, and no per-binding queue or action limits.
change_notes.new: Revision 2 freezes entity-scoped create, replace, and runtime-state APIs under the entity execution role; each binding carries canonical action and queue limits, due interval and escalation maximum, optimistic versions, and least-privilege automation role checks.
change_notes.authorization: The requesting contract owner confirmed approval to change the shared contract in this session.
change_notes.compatibility: Retire revision 1 binding-administration APIs. Preserve existing binding and receipt history; pause existing bindings until an operator replaces and explicitly activates a fully bounded revision 2 binding.

runtime_relation.logical_dump: Do not dump runtime rows; restore begins disabled.

invariants: At most one unreplaced binding exists per entity and automation role name.
The automation role must be NOLOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, and NOBYPASSRLS, have no membership path to the helper or entity execution role, and retain the same stored name and OID at intent time.

Action and queue arrays are canonical and duplicate-free. ASSIGN_QUEUE requires a nonempty queue allowlist; SET_DUE_AT requires a positive max_due_interval; ESCALATE requires a positive max_escalation_level.

Replacement creates a fresh inactive binding and permanently marks the prior binding replaced with replaced_by and replaced_at. Old receipts remain attached to the old binding and are replayable only after caller authentication.
Logical restore leaves runtime activation absent or disabled. A physical clone fails the database OID check. Explicit entity-execution-role reconciliation is required before new intents apply.

administrator_surface.create: mdm_admin.create_policy_binding(entity_name text, automation_role_name text, policy_digest bytea, allowed_actions text[], allowed_queues name[], max_due_interval interval, max_escalation_level integer) returns (binding_id uuid, binding_version bigint). Creates a binding and active runtime row at version one.
administrator_surface.replace: mdm_admin.replace_policy_binding(binding_id uuid, expected_version bigint, policy_digest bytea, allowed_actions text[], allowed_queues name[], max_due_interval interval, max_escalation_level integer) returns (binding_id uuid, binding_version bigint). Marks the old binding replaced and creates a fresh inactive binding.
administrator_surface.state: mdm_admin.set_policy_binding_state(binding_id uuid, expected_runtime_version bigint, state text, reason text) returns runtime_version bigint. Supports activation, pause, and explicit database/role OID reconciliation.
administrator_surface.authorization: Only the owning entity execution role may create, replace, activate, pause, or reconcile its bindings through fixed-path MDM helpers with optimistic version checks.
administrator_surface.react_access: React has no direct SELECT or DML on this relation; the bound role may call submit_policy_intent only. No PUBLIC grants.

bindings.legacy_transition: Revision 1 binding-administration functions are revoked and retired. Existing bindings and receipts are retained; existing runtime is paused. An old binding can be replaced with fully bounded revision 2 settings and explicitly activated. Existing request keys and receipts are never transferred.
bindings.submit_behavior: Authenticate the caller against the binding's stored role name and current role OID before receipt lookup. An identical authorized prior request returns its original receipt after pause or replacement; a new request on a paused or replaced binding receives BINDING_PAUSED or BINDING_REPLACED with no control change.

freshness.stewardship_epoch_meaning: The decision_epoch associated with the latest successful observation. It may be older than the current entity decision_epoch; pending_stewardship is true in that case.
freshness.review_version_meaning: The exact concurrency_version of the mdm_out.<entity>_review row for this case's review_id.
freshness.pending_stewardship_rule: If pending_stewardship is true at intent validation, deny the control with terminal outcome PENDING_STEWARDSHIP and make no control change. It may proceed only after a successful observation clears pending_stewardship.
freshness.action_revision: Increment only when evidence or an action control can change policy eligibility or result. Observation timestamps, receipt writes, and unrelated publication advances do not increment it.

intent.signature: mdm_steward.submit_policy_intent(binding_id uuid, request_key bytea, case_key bigint, action text, arguments jsonb, expected_review_version bigint, expected_definition_version bigint, expected_publication_revision bigint, expected_stewardship_epoch bigint, expected_evidence_basis_digest bytea, expected_action_revision bigint, expected_policy_digest bytea, policy_revision text, evaluation_ref text, work_ref text)
intent.actor_capture: The invoker-facing SQL wrapper captures current_user at entry and passes it to fixed-path privileged helpers. The public signature has no actor parameter.

request_key.encoding: React derives the key from the request_key_vector using canonical_encoding.version. case_key identifies one immutable review occurrence. lifecycle_generation starts at 1 and increases only when React starts a new work lifecycle for that case; retries keep it unchanged. escalation_level is the target level for ESCALATE and zero for other actions.
inputs: non-empty UTF-8 text, at most 256 bytes
non-empty UTF-8 text, at most 256 bytes
nonnegative integer; zero except for ESCALATE

policy_digest.owner: React computes the digest; MDM treats it as opaque and compares the exact bytes with the active binding's policy_digest.
policy_digest.preimage: The canonical JSON object contains canonical_encoding_version, policy_revision, and the complete normalized policy_package used to derive routing, deadline, and escalation intents. Deployment metadata, evaluation_ref, work_ref, runtime timestamps, and secrets are excluded.

intent.references: policy_revision, evaluation_ref, work_ref are non-empty text, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.
intent.argument_keys: Each action accepts exactly its listed keys; extra keys, null values, and wrong JSON types are rejected.

idempotency.authorization: Authenticate and validate the binding before looking up a receipt.
idempotency.same_body: For the same binding_id, request_key, and canonical request digest, return the original receipt without repeating the control change.
idempotency.concurrent_insert: After a unique-key conflict, read the existing receipt and compare request digests. Return that receipt for an equal body or the changed_body response for a different body. Never replace the existing row or retry with a new key.

intent.publication: Every v1 intent has resulting_publication_revision null. Accepted control changes do not resolve identity or publish MDM output.
intent.authority: The bound automation role may submit only the three typed actions. It cannot decide, override golden values, refresh, rebuild, merge, split, or approve.
intent.receipts: Create one immutable receipt for each first authorized request, including terminal validation outcomes. Replays return that receipt. IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT is returned without a receipt row.

canonical_encoding.json: UTF-8 compact JSON; object keys sorted by UTF-8 byte order; array order preserved; strings use RFC 8259 escaping; numbers are base-10 integers without leading zeroes; floating point values are forbidden.
canonical_encoding.digest: SHA-256 over each part framed by an unsigned 32-bit big-endian byte length. First part is the UTF-8 domain tag, second part is the canonical JSON bytes.
canonical_encoding.intent_request_body: Contains every submit_policy_intent input except request_key. The request_key is the idempotency lookup key and is not included in the body digest.

shared_conformance_cases: React derives the same request key when it retries the same persisted work.
The same binding, request key, and body return the original immutable receipt.
A changed body with the same binding and request key returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT with a null receipt_id; it leaves the stored receipt unchanged and creates no row.
Concurrent submissions with the same key return the original receipt for an equal body and the conflict response for a different body.
The receipt actor is the authenticated effective database role captured by MDM; the caller cannot provide it.
Stale review, definition, publication basis, stewardship epoch, evidence digest, action revision, or policy digest cannot apply a control.
A newer unrelated publication does not stale an unchanged case basis.
Manual assignment protection denies automatic queue replacement.
Pause, binding replacement, and policy mismatch create the specified terminal outcome.
Receipt and control change commit atomically or both roll back.
Resolved occurrences remain readable and recurrence gets a new case key.
Restore preserves case keys, request bodies, and receipts.
A case with pending_stewardship cannot receive control until a successful observation clears it.
Only the entity execution role can create, replace, activate, pause, or reconcile bindings; automation role mismatch and replaced bindings fail closed.
